**24 palavras novas** (filosofia).

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C2):** eu consigo ler, ouvir, falar e escrever um conto filosófico a partir do paradoxo de Zenão, usando discurso indireto e marcação de fala, com ritmo narrativo adequado.

body: Esta aula treina **ouvir e anotar informações (IELTS Listening, TOEFL Listening)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Achilles at the Tram Stop
paras: Achilles, **late for the last tram**, found the Tortoise already on the platform. “You **will never** catch it either,” **the Tortoise remarked**, **gesturing** at the empty rails. Achilles **replied that** he had **run** the whole way. The Tortoise **observed that** to reach the stop he must first have **covered half** the distance, **then half of what was left**, and so on **without end**.

Achilles **thought for a moment**. “**But here I am**,” he **said**. The Tortoise **admitted** that this was the **troublesome** part. **The tram, meanwhile**, **rounded the corner**; neither of them had **noticed** that it had **arrived** at last. **“Sums can wait,”** said Achilles, **stepping aboard**.

items.q: The Tortoise argues that Achilles must cover infinitely many distances.
items.why: half… then half of what was left.

items.q: The story is set in ancient Greece.
items.why: Only a tram stop is mentioned; the setting’s era is not stated.

head: Direto
Indireto
Verbo
rows: He replied **that** he **had run** the whole way.
The Tortoise remarked **that** he **would never** catch it.
The Tortoise admitted **that this was** the troublesome part.

blocks.body: No discurso indireto, o verbo **recua um tempo** (*have run → had run*; *will → would*; *can → could*), e os dêiticos mudam (*here → there*, *now → then*). Verbos como **observe, admit, remark** colorem a atitude.
Em narrativa, o diálogo direto aparece entre aspas com **marcação de fala** (*he said*, *the Tortoise remarked*). Evite repetir *said* em excesso.

items.s: Achilles replied that he ___ run the whole way. (have)
The Tortoise remarked that he ___ never catch it. (will)
The Tortoise ___ that this was the troublesome part. (admit)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

body: **Catch up with.** — Alcançar.
**Miss the boat.** — Perder a oportunidade.
**Just in the nick of time.** — No último instante.
**Run out of time.** — Ficar sem tempo.
**Cut it fine.** — Chegar em cima da hora.
**Beat the clock.** — Vencer o relógio.
**Hold up.** — Atrasar.
**Step aboard.** — Embarcar.
**Tortoise and hare.** — Tartaruga e lebre.
**Make up for lost time.** — Recuperar o tempo perdido.
**And what did Achilles reply?** — E o que Aquiles respondeu?
**Why did the Tortoise say Achilles would never catch it?** — Por que a Tartaruga disse que Aquiles nunca pegaria?
**That sums could wait, and he boarded the tram.** — Que as contas podiam esperar, e embarcou no bonde.

forms: Corredores mais rápidos ultrapassam os lentos.

blocks.title: Pronúncia: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances

items.label: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances
items.note: Ritmo e ênfase para nuances: o acento muda o sentido (He said she STOLE it × he said SHE stole it) e as pausas separam ideias técnicas densas.
words: I didn’t SAY he did it.
I didn’t say HE did it.
I didn’t say he DID it.

prompts.model: He replied that he had run the whole way.
The Tortoise observed that the distance was infinite.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence story scene using at least four reporting verbs and indirect speech.
blocks.model: Maria told the clerk that she had lost her ticket. The clerk replied that rules were rules. She explained that the train had been late. He admitted that the delay was not her fault. He stamped a new ticket, remarking that kindness was cheaper than paperwork. She smiled and boarded.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
